<a name="member-copy-28--29-"></a>

### `copy()`

```java
public ArrayList<E> copy()
```

Copies ordered membership into independent mutable storage.



The result owns its array and reusable iterator, with the default
growth factor and initial capacity equal to the larger of one and this
list's size. Unused source capacity is not copied.
Elements are borrowed, retain their identity and are never destroyed by
this operation or either list's destructor. Null elements cannot occur
in a valid list. The source iterator's position is unchanged.



This operation takes linear time and allocates one list, one iterator,
and one backing array for an ordinary list. On failure all result storage is
reclaimed and source membership is unchanged. Free the result only after
its last consumer; keep its borrowed elements alive until then.

**Returns**

a fresh mutable list with the same ordered element references


[Back to member summary](#member-summary)

<a name="member-sortWithComparator-28-Comparator-3c--3f--20-super-20-E-3e--29-"></a>

### `sortWithComparator(Comparator<? super E>)`

```java
public void sortWithComparator(Comparator<? super E> comparator)
```

Sorts the live elements stably with an explicit comparator.



Only indexes `[0, size())` are compared and reordered. Elements
the comparator considers equal keep their encounter order. Size,
capacity, growth factor and the reusable iterator's position are
unchanged, elements keep their identity and none is freed. The
comparator is required even for an empty list; unlike Java's
`List.sort`, there is no natural-order fallback.



The sort takes O(n log n) comparisons, or n - 1 for already sorted
input. Lists of at most sixteen elements are sorted without workspace;
a longer list allocates one private array of `size() / 2`
references and frees it before returning, also on failure. If the
comparator throws, the exception propagates and the list holds the same
elements in an unspecified order. A comparator that mutates this list
leaves its order unspecified; the comparator must not do so.

**Parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `comparator` | the ordering; it may retain or publish the elements it compares, so its actual effects govern their lifetime |

**Throws**

| Exception | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| [`NullPointerException`](../lang/NullPointerException.md) | if `comparator` is null |
